title: What If Every Krill in the Ocean Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every krill vanished? They're smaller than your finger, yet whales depend on them.
Krill swarms can hold up to 30 trillion animals, each only about six centimeters long.
They feed whales, seals, penguins, fish, and squid. Remove that bottom link, and the animals above it lose a main meal.
Krill also eat tiny ocean plants, then sink their waste deep. That locks away at least 20 million tonnes of carbon every year.
That waste can stay stored for more than a century, at an average depth of about 380 meters.
Smaller than your finger, krill feed the biggest animals on Earth and help bury carbon too.
